task: Author request: review the features5 logs (turn-based and real time, one session) for bad or broken decisions and functionality gaps, and bugfix (evidence-based, high-performance, feasible and integrated)
author: Claude

inputs.commands: turn-based 209 issued; real-time 426 issued, 415 ended: 258 success, 33 interrupted after acting, 122 before acting, 2 fail
inputs.note: Raw logs stay private; only their fingerprints are recorded. The author confirmed Camellia's other weapon set holds a starknife (melee).

findings_fixed: Both modes (performance, same numbers): real-time fights 7 and 12 (42 and 47 enemies) had four decisions over 1 s, the slowest 2,069 ms (640 ms in the previous log). Approach planning took 400-950 ms of them (195-242 approaches a decision): every priced spot read each ally's drop chance against every enemy, with native reads of the enemy's melee weapon, reach and lying-down state per pair. The drop table now reads each enemy's strike data once (ReadStrike, RowStrikeShare), an ally's share where it stands once (OwnStrikeShare), and a walk re-reads only the allies an enemy whose target choice it changes can pick (MoverChangedRows, ChangeTouches; every ally with a swarm in the fight). Lists reused; ValueModel.CombinedDrop(List) without an enumerator. The slow row names drop-chance reads, time and skipped allies.

Real time: an ability that walks to its target first (around an area, to a free side, to touch range) was not a cast command, so CombatMemory.CastPendingByOther did not see it: the Vrock, a Shadow Demon and Seelah each walked to the same helpless Nabasu for a Coup de Grace (fight 9). Such a walk now counts as the cast while it runs (NotePendingWalk); its end clears it.

Log and saves: every Magic Fusion is cast through one native holder ability with no name. [Save] rows read "Knight Commander's : ..." (69 rows) and observations (a target's automatic pass or contextual bonus) were shared by every fusion. Rows now name the fusion (AbilityData.Name) and observations and fight tallies are kept per fusion (AbilityProfile.FusionIdentityOf).

features5_observed.weapon_sets: The Bandit switched to his Light Crossbow +5 set twice in turn-based mode (move action, then the attack) and kept it; no switch back offered (crossbow priced above the Shortsword +1). Camellia: no ranged weapon in another set (a starknife, melee; author).
features5_observed.redecisions: no option dropped to decide again was barred afterwards; the Vrock's Stunning Screech dropped at 73 -> 20 HP was chosen again
features5_observed.provoke_redecision: once (fight 10): a Quickwood Sprout reached a Nabasu walking to a Coup de Grace; the new decision priced the attacks of opportunity and chose Enervation

observed_not_changed: Six real-time coups de grace issued, none delivered (all interrupted before acting). The Nabasu was held by Phantasmal Web (entangled, cannot move); its state at the coup is not in the log (Tabletop Tweaks' coup). Holding other attacks off a coup target is a commitment change for the author.
Five Cure Critical Wounds on Seelah in two bursts (fight 9) all healed in full (about 150 max HP): no waste, no heal coordination added.
70 commands ended before acting with no AI Control reason (66 real-time); samples checked came as the target died.
Turn-based Vrock full attacks with a step needing 2.5-8 m were withheld by the path check before issue; the next option was taken.

checks.profile_audit: exit 0; new V0370-FEATURES5 10 checks passed (call routes, the native Coup de Grace target restriction, the skip's TargetChance ground); every other report line identical to features5
